subject: FleetFlow: sudden p99 latency + 502s on streaming ingest — urgent
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@fleetflow.com>
To: support@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@fleetflow.com
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p99 latency + 502s on streaming ingest — urgent

Hi Redwood team,

We're seeing a sharp spike in p99 latency on our streaming ingest since ~08:55 PT and about 18% of requests are returning 502/timeout. This is hitting our live routing and causing queuing at the edge — affect is visible across multiple regions (US-west p95 -> p99 delta ~900ms). We rolled a config tweak on our side (reduced batch size) but no change.

Attached are a short pcap and a trace slice (heapshot-0503.pcap, trace-20280503.json). The traffic pattern appears normal but the SDK client suddenly began retrying heavily and the server reports many "malformed header" parse errors.

Can you triage asap? We're blocking on this for a large launch this morning.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform
FleetFlow Inc

From: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer, marissa_cole, aditya_rao
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: sudden p99 latency + 502s on streaming ingest — triage notes

Folks — quick notes from initial triage (pulling on traces + logs):
- We see repeated "header-fragmentation" parse failures in the streaming parser when client packets contain a contiguous metadata blob > 24KB. Parser treats trailing bytes as a new header boundary and raises a recoverable parse error that currently triggers a retry path.
- The retry backoff combined with partial KV cache invalidation is amplifying downstream latency.
- Affected flow predominantly from the FleetFlow SDK v2.3.1 (they included user-agent in traces).

Immediate mitigation available:
1) Toggle streaming->batch ingestion fallback on the route (reduces p99 but increases per-request token cost).
2) Patch the streaming parser to be tolerant of large single-header metadata (hotfix) — low-risk but needs a short deploy window.

I'll attach a small repro trace and an exec summary for Lauren.

Attachments: sdk-log-0504.txt

Rachel
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

- Rachel, please schedule the parser patch as a hotfix (priority P1). We should aim for a 30-minute slot and include a rollback plan.
- Karthik, recommend we offer FleetFlow a 10% credit for the hours impacted and a customer-facing postmortem within 48 hours.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@fleetflow.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer, marissa_cole, rachel_kim
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 latency + 502s on streaming ingest — mitigation underway

Hi Samantha — quick update from Redwood: we've spun up a controlled fallback route that moves ~70% of FleetFlow traffic off the streaming parser. You should see reduced errors and improved tail latency.

Our engineering team has identified the likely root cause as fragmentation of single large metadata headers exceeding the streaming parser's internal buffer assumptions. We're preparing a small server-side fix and a clarifying SDK recommendation (limit metadata blobs or upgrade to v2.3.2 which includes a client-side mitigation) — ETA for hotfix deploy: 60–90 minutes.

We're also opening an ops ticket to review retry/backoff knobs to avoid cascading retries in future. I'll confirm a maintenance window once the fix is ready.

Thanks for your patience — we'll keep you posted every 30 minutes.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Technical Lead, Customer Integrations
Redwood Inference
